text:
ian: Heads up — we're seeing a cluster-wide spike in Provisioning/Pending for GPU pods in us-west2. ~30 pods Pending. Nodes reporting sustained high iowait and kernel messages about IO quota. Some batch jobs stuck in scheduling backpressure.

maya: same. scheduler backlog growth, GPU nodes flapping DiskPressure briefly. Noticed ephemeral-cleaner kicked off around 10:12 UTC on many nodes.

sam: quick snapshot from gnode-07:
```
iostat -x 1 3
nvme0n1: r/s 7200 w/s 120, await 11.2 svctm 9.8 %util 99.9
kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
```
qdepth looks saturated, latency >10ms on many reqs.

infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_iostat high on gnode-07 (threshold 4000 r/s) — auto-scale attempt triggered.

chris: Plan: cordon + drain the top offenders, reduce ephemeral-cleaner concurrency, and add a short delay between deletes. Also consider setting per-node iops caps or changing io_scheduler to reduce tail latency.

maya: also seeing dmesg spam: "nvme nvme0: I/O queue timeout" on a couple nodes. Not promoting to read-only yet but counters creeping.

ian: I'll make an evict list: gnode-07, gnode-12, gnode-21. Sam, can you cordon/drain those and kick provisioning fallback to eu-west1 if we can't reclaim capacity?

sam: starting cordon+drain gnode-07: `kubectl drain gnode-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will prefer reschedule to other zones, but if not possible we fallback to dedicated pool.

oncall: FYI — avoid draining nodes that are mid-batch if possible. Prefer partial reschedule. If we shift GPUs to Dedicated pool, estimated incremental cost ~+$1.2k/day for +150 GPUs. Flagging finance.

chris: quick mitigation applied: updated ConfigMap `ephemeral-cleaner` concurrency -> 2 and insert 30s delay between deletions. Also applied `echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` on candidate nodes to reduce variance.

sam: made the config change and rolled to nodes in us-west2. Initial metrics: gnode-07 r/s dropped 7200 -> ~1500, latency 11ms -> ~3ms.

maya: good — hold on mass drains for 30m and monitor dmesg / S.M.A.R.T counters.

ian: created incident doc (link: https://go/incident/2250004321) and assigned owners: chris (mitigation), sam (drain + provisioning), maya (forensics/logs). Flagged potential customer impact to SRE leads.

infra-bot: AUTOSCALE: started 50 spot-provision attempts in us-west2, 6 succeeded, 44 pending due to local-disk resource constraint.

chris: if spots keep failing, fallback zone is eu-west1-b (prefer latency for batch). Also adding anti-affinity rule to avoid packing GPU + hottest NVMe in same rack — reduces throughput density but limits single-rack blast radius.

sam: monitoring now, will post updates every 10m. :thumbsup:

oncall: note — we should run a postmortem for the cleaner release that increased concurrency last week. If this is correlated, we'll pin cleaner to previous config and add a canary flag.

chris: Agreed. I'll open a PR to add a rate-limit feature to the cleaner and a preflight check that scans recent IO metrics before allowing concurrency=high.

sam: continuing to watch iostat and scheduler backlog, will update when drains finish or if provisioning completes.
